subject: Post-call: Clarify regional SLOs & data residency for Acme Retail POC
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Clarify regional SLOs & data residency for Acme Retail POC

Thanks Jane — great call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have the requirements captured for the POC and the upcoming tech deep dive.

Recap (what we heard)
- Traffic distribution: US-heavy, some EU and APAC; exact percentages to confirm.
- Performance targets: Acme asks for p95 latency budget in each region (you suggested target ranges during the call).
- Functional needs: streaming token-level responses for chat UX, per-tenant data residency controls, and predictable throughput at peak.
- Constraints: EU data must remain in-region; APAC may require a VPC/private deployment option.

Questions we need answered to size the POC and finalize the SLOs
1) Approx peak RPS and typical request size (tokens in/out).
2) Expected concurrency per user and global concurrency headroom.
3) Percent of traffic by region (approx).
4) Is cross-region failover acceptable if the primary region is unavailable, or is strict in-region processing required for some flows?

Suggested initial SLO band (for discussion in tech deep dive)
- US: p95 <= 120 ms (inferred response time for non-streaming short prompts), p50 token-latency for streaming <40 ms
- EU: p95 <= 160 ms, p50 token-latency for streaming <60 ms
- APAC: p95 <= 220 ms with hosted routing; or p95 <= 140 ms if APAC-dedicated/Dedicated VPC is provisioned
- Throughput: baseline target 200–500 RPS depending on model; need final numbers from you to size autoscaling
- Concurrency: support bursts to 1k concurrent requests across tenants during peak; recommend 50–100 concurrent requests per instance for linear scaling

Attachments: redwood-slo-summary.xlsx (summary table), network-topology-diagram.pdf (what we need from your infra team)

Next steps
- Jane: please confirm traffic split, peak RPS, and strictness of residency requirements.
- Redwood: we will share a short network checklist and a draft POC plan (+ cost/estimate).
- Schedule tech deep dive w/ Vivek and our runtime team — propose Fri 07/31 or Mon 08/03.

Thanks again — looking forward to the deep dive.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Jane Park <jane.park@acme-retail.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Retail Platform Team <platform@acme-retail.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:04:23 +0100
Subject: Re: Post-call: Clarify regional SLOs & data residency for Acme Retail POC

Hi Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

Traffic & load
- Estimated steady-state: ~120 RPS globally.
- Peak (Black Friday test / marketing bursts): ~600 RPS sustained for ~5 minutes with spikes to 900 RPS.
- Typical prompt sizes: 60–160 tokens in, expect ~100–300 tokens out for our assistant flows.
- Concurrency: concurrent user sessions typically 4–8 per active user; we plan for 800 concurrent sessions in the POC.

Regional split (approx)
- US: 62%
- EU: 28% (primarily Germany, NL)
- APAC: 10% (mostly Singapore/Japan)

Residency / compliance
- EU customer data (including prompts and logs) must remain in EU for regulated cohorts. Some non-sensitive inference can fall back out-of-region if explicitly allowed.
- For APAC we prefer VPC/private deployment; hosted is acceptable for the POC if network egress remains in-region but production will probably require Private.

Latency expectations (what our PM suggested internally)
- US: p95 < 120 ms for short prompts; streaming token latency p50 < 45 ms
- EU: p95 < 180 ms; streaming p50 < 70 ms
- APAC: p95 < 250 ms (we know this is challenging)

Questions for Redwood
1) Can you confirm streaming support (token-level flush) with <50 ms p50 in US under 200 RPS?
2) How does fallback routing work if EU region capacity is exhausted — do requests route to US or fail?
3) For APAC private deployments, what is the expected lead time and what components need to be on-prem vs in VPC?

We can do the tech deep dive on Fri 07/31 10:00–11:00 PT. Please include your runtime/infra lead for kernel/quantization questions.

Thanks,
Jane Park
Head of Platform Integrations | Acme Retail
jane.park@acme-retail.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:45:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Clarify regional SLOs & data residency for Acme Retail POC

Jane — great, this is exactly the detail we need. Quick answers and proposed approach below so we can lock the POC scope before Friday's deep dive.

Short answers
1) Streaming: Yes, Redwood supports token-level streaming. In our hosted environment we routinely hit token p50 < 40–50 ms in US under 150–200 RPS with appropriate batching/windowing settings.
2) Fallback routing: By default we route by policy; for strict residency flows we will not failover out-of-region unless you opt into cross-region fallback. We can configure a per-route policy: strict-in-region vs best-effort routing.
3) APAC private: lead time typically 6–10 weeks depending on procurement and network setup. For POC we can provide a dedicated APAC region pool (hosted) and a Private option for production. Components usually: inference runtime and model cache in customer VPC, control plane in a private-managed instance or dedicated region, KMS integration for keys.

Suggested SLOs (draft, will validate in POC)
- US hosted: p95 <= 120 ms (short prompts), streaming token p50 <= 45 ms; supports 200–500 RPS with autoscaling and prefix KV caching.
- EU hosted (+EU residency mode): p95 <= 170 ms; streaming token p50 <= 65 ms; strict-in-region policy prevents cross-region routing for designated routes.
- APAC hosted: p95 <= 220–260 ms depending on model size; recommend Dedicated APAC pool for p95 <= 140 ms if you need consistently low latency.

Operational notes
- Batching window: small windows (10–25 ms) for chat workloads to keep token latency low; we’ll tune during the POC.
- KV / prefix caching: can reduce tokens emitted and improve p95 significantly for repeated prompts. We recommend identifying hot prompt families for the POC.
- Quantization/model variants: we can propose a lower-cost quantized variant for APAC to reduce latency if Dedicated GPUs are limited.

Next steps before Fri deep dive
- We will share: network checklist, redwood-slo-summary.xlsx with per-region targets and a simple canary plan, and a short doc on residency routing policies. (attached)
- Vivek, please add any infra caveats or required telemetry hooks for the POC.

Thanks — see you on Fri.

Best,
Priyom

Attachments: redwood-slo-summary.xlsx (attached)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0400
Subject: Internal: Prep notes for Acme POC deep dive (Fri)

Quick internal notes before the call — do not forward to customer.

- Bring runtime owner (I will) and the engineer who owns streaming path and KV cache.
- Ask Acme for a 3-hour maintenance window to run a controlled load test that mirrors their Black Friday peak (we need to validate autoscaling and canary rollback).
- From infra: request egress IP ranges and expected TLS termination flow (we will provide our network checklist).
- If Acme insists on strict EU in-region processing for logs + prompts, we need to scope where logs are written and whether we can support aggregated telemetry across regions without moving raw prompts. Consider pseudonymization for telemetry.
- APAC: start a parallel thread with PM about lead time and procurement checklist for Dedicated VPC; historic experience is 6–10 weeks.

Agenda for Fri
1) Confirm traffic numbers and region distribution (Jane)
2) Walk POC plan and canary plan (Priyom)
3) Runtime deep dive on streaming & batching (Vivek)
4) Residency policy and telemetry (Marissa)

I'll join the Fri 10:00 PT slot. Priyom, can you send the calendar invite and include links to the shared Drive assets?

-Vivek
Senior Director, Runtime | Redwood Inference
